title: They’re Lying To You About Debt... Here's How To Get Rich | Robert Kiyosaki
summary: A best-selling real-estate author argues houses are not assets, savers lose to fiat inflation, bank debt on cash-flowing rentals builds wealth, and schools teach nothing useful about money.

assertions.quote: It has to do with this thing called cash flow.

verdicts.note: A house is an asset by any accounting definition; the cash-flow framing is a redefinition, though it correctly warns that an owner-occupied home costs money rather than paying it.

assertions.quote: Rich don't save money because I savers are losers because you're saving fake money.

verdicts.note: Inflation does erode idle cash, but an emergency fund and savings rate are the strongest predictors of household wealth; 'savers are losers' is wrong as advice.

assertions.quote: and then use the real estate to provide cash flow, not income. cash flow. So, today I own what? 15,000 rental properties.

verdicts.note: Leveraged rentals have built real fortunes, but leverage magnifies losses equally and many highly leveraged small landlords were wiped out in 2008 and by rate rises.

assertions.quote: When you go to school, you're lectured to by somebody is not even rich.

verdicts.note: Personal-finance education is thin in most curricula, but educational attainment remains one of the strongest predictors of lifetime income and wealth.

assertions.quote: If it doesn't make money, don't buy it. And you stay there until you can have it make money.

verdicts.note: Negative-cash-flow 'value-add' deals do fail often, but renovation plays can work when underwritten carefully; the rule is conservative rather than universal.

assertions.quote: The reason you're failing is because you're not failing fast enough. If you're going to fail, step up your failure rate.

verdicts.note: Motivational framing; more attempts do mechanically produce more sales, but 'failure rate' is not a measurable cause.

The model's individual-level lesson is that since lucky events cannot be controlled, the best strategy at any talent level is to broaden activity and output to maximise exposure to lucky events; it does not model learning from failure.

assertions.quote: what the hand does, the mind remembers, cash flow is the only board game that teaches you accounting.

verdicts.note: Active learning does outperform lectures in education research, but there is no independent evidence that this particular product improves financial outcomes.

assertions.quote: 15,000 time 200. I wasn't good at math, but that's more than what school teachers make.

verdicts.note: At portfolio scale rentals do out-earn salaries, but the claim skips the decades of capital, leverage and operating risk needed to get there; self-reported holdings are unverified.
